messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test asserts that NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizer updates its iteration count (MATH-949): optimizer.getIterations() > 0.

What happens in the code:
- BaseOptimizer.getIterations() returns the value of an internal counter (iterations.getCount()).
- That counter is reset to zero at the beginning of each optimization run in BaseOptimizer.optimize(...):
  - evaluations.resetCount();
  - iterations.resetCount();
- The counter is only advanced when BaseOptimizer.incrementIterationCount() is called.

In NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizer.doOptimize(), the optimizer uses its own local iteration variable:
- A local int iter is declared and incremented (++iter) inside the main optimization loop.
- This local iter is used for the convergence checker (checker.converged(iter, previous, current)).
- However, there is no call to BaseOptimizer.incrementIterationCount() anywhere in doOptimize().

Consequence:
- Since BaseOptimizer.optimize resets the iterations counter to 0 and NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizer never increments it, getIterations() always returns 0 after optimize(...), even though iterations actually occurred. This directly causes the test’s final assertion (optimizer.getIterations() > 0) to fail.

This is consistent with the broader issue described in the bug report: some optimizers fail to propagate their internal iteration progress to BaseOptimizer’s iteration counter. Here, NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizer maintains a local count but does not update the shared counter.

Root cause:
- Missing calls to BaseOptimizer.incrementIterationCount() within NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizer.doOptimize(), where a local iteration counter is used instead.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
